output.brief: The August drop is real but narrow. It sits on floors 6-8 and tracks the chiller failure: CH-2 was down from 4 to 19 August, and floors 6-8 ran at 26-30 C while the score there fell to about 6.8 for guests checking out 5-20 August. Floors 1-5 stayed cool and scored normally. Once the chiller was fixed, floors 6-8 recovered to 8.4-8.6. The survey itself did not change, and housekeeping pass rates and cleanliness scores held steady, so the new contractor and the kiosks look unlikely to be the cause. The rate rise may have nudged value-for-money scores, but nothing in the data separates it from the usual August dip. I am fairly confident about the chiller cause and less sure about the rate effect. Next steps: reschedule the deferred maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spare parts, and write a cooling-outage guest recovery protocol. Do not serve notice on Orrin or pull the kiosks on this evidence. Do not drop the August figures from the score. Consider a return-stay offer for floors 6-8 guests from the outage period.
